commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 (PR #1300): removes hard-coded exemplar entry_is_line_a..e derived rules (proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines) from every generated chapter and makes them caller inputs; summary claims runtime semantics unchanged — unsure, part of the same decoupling repair.
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The chapter 50 composition gated its section 301, section 338 and surcharge carve-out branches on hard-coded identity tests for HTS lines in chapters 22, 72, 76, 85 and 95, conditions ungrounded in chapter 50's source and impossible for any chapter 50 entry to satisfy.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 48 (identical two-hunk shape: summary regeneration plus removal of entry_is_line_a..e; only the redundant-parenthesis padding count and the from/effective_from spelling differ per chapter). Diff read in full; no other formulas, parameters, dates, or outputs changed in this module.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as mechanical or as a scaffold enhancement and could not: the diff deletes five derived rules whose formulas were hard-coded identity tests on statistical reporting numbers from chapters 72, 76, 95, 22 and 85 (e.g. `hts_number == "7202.11.10.00"`), each carrying proof atoms citing those other chapters' provisions, from a chapter 50 (silk) composition where no entry can ever satisfy them, while every formula that consumes those flags (the §301 stack at `if entry_is_line_a and origin_is_china: list_1_additional_ad_valorem_rate`, the §338 beer branch, and the §122 surcharge carve-out `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0`) is left untouched. The cited overlay text in the same module states membership semantics — "Heading 9903.88.03 applies to all products of China that are classified in the following 8-digit subheadings" — so gating those branches on five exemplar line identities is a condition with no basis in the provisions the module cites, and the fix re-grounds the identifiers as caller inputs "supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification." Encoded meaning, not just bookkeeping, changes: the module's input surface gains five inputs and the companion test drops the `positive coverage: entry_is_line_a` cases that fed a chapter-72 `hts_number` into a chapter 50 module, replacing them with `#input.entry_is_line_a` assignments. That is the untraceable_branch pattern (branch grounded on the wrong provision, removed/re-grounded by the fix), not amount, boundary, polarity, period, or a missing clause.
triage.verifier_notes: Checked pre (parent 956a547418) and post ch50.yaml directly: the only changes are the summary rewrite and removal of entry_is_line_a..e; all 18 referencing formula sites are byte-identical across the commit (pre lines 2007/2467/2672/2748/2844/2916/3094-3098/3139/3297 vs post 1907/2367/2572/2648/2744/2816/2994-2998/3039/3197). The steel component and the §122 decoupling onto `entry_is_section_122_exempt` described in the PR body are NOT in this commit for ch50 — they land elsewhere in the stack, so this commit is stage 1 (removing the ungrounded definitions) of the repair. The honest counterargument a reviewer should weigh: the generated module declares itself a deterministic copy of the hand-built five-line witness pilot ("copies the witness's authority components, declared-entry variants, proof atoms, formulas, inputs"), and both pre and post summaries carry boilerplate claiming "runtime semantics are unchanged," so one could read this as architectural decoupling / coverage expansion rather than correcting a claim the module made. I weighted against that because the deleted rules are conditions ungrounded in chapter 50's source that made every §301/§338 branch dead for the whole chapter, and because the PR body names the lawfulness failure ("round-2 evaluation showed unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins"). Also note the post header still lists us/statute/hts/7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 9506.62.40.40, 2203.00.00.30 and 8541.42.00.10 in source_verification because surviving component atoms still cite them; that residue is not evidence the removal was cosmetic. Did not need the corpus resolver: the kind turns on which provision the branch is grounded in, which the in-module proof atoms settle, not on a number or boundary in the source text. All commands were read-only (git show / sed / grep on single files).
